Hi Daniel & Sofia,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the internal search/knowledge pipeline and the primary user flows (support triage, contract lookup, and onboarding KB). Quick recap + recommended next steps from our side so we can move to a focused POC: 

Recap / priority areas
- Primary objectives: improve grounding for contract answers, keep latency under 400ms p50 for short queries, and reduce hallucination in legal Q&A.
- Data: ~1.2M docs (contracts + KB), incremental daily updates from S3, current vector store: Pinecone (we noted it's on a paid plan).

Redwood recommended starting config (POC baseline)
- Candidate models: redwood-7b-q (quantized) for low-latency arm; redwood-13b-std for accuracy arm; cross-encoder reranker (redwood-reranker-v2) as a downstream re-rank.
- Retrieval settings: chunk_size=500 tokens, overlap=50, embed_model=redwood-embed-2, vector_top_k=50, reranker_top_n=5.
- Caching: prefix caching enabled for repeated contract queries.
- Grounding/metrics to track: precision@1, MRR, grounding_rate (answers with cited doc id), hallucination_rate (manual eval spot checks). Target: precision@1 >= 0.92 for primary queries, hallucination_rate < 3%.

Attachments: acme_rag_eval_summary.pdf (high-level config + benchmarks), prompt-sets.csv (initial prompt/test sets we discussed).

Proposed next steps
1) Quick internal benchmark: Redwood runs a 48-hour batch benchmark against a 1k-sample prompt set (we can use the prompt-sets.csv attached).
2) Align on two POC arms (low-latency vs high-accuracy).
3) Follow-up call to agree on success criteria and SOW: Tue, Nov 24 or Wed, Nov 25 — what works for you?

Action items for ACME
- Share a representative 1000-query prompt set and two redacted contract samples for benchmarking (S3 link or share via Drive).
- Confirm whether you prefer Pinecone or an alternative vector store for the POC (we can support both).

I'll loop Vivek in on the retrieval/reranker specifics below.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick tech notes to answer Daniel and to provide a recommended test matrix.

Reranker behavior & cost
- The cross-encoder reranker is an additional model call that scores candidate passages against the query. In practice: retrieval (dense retriever) -> top_k (50) -> cross-encoder rerank top_k -> return top_n (5).
- Latency impact: reranker adds ~50-120ms p50 per query when run on a GPU-accelerated instance (depends on model size). On CPU the cost/latency rises significantly — we recommend GPU for the reranker in the accuracy arm.
- Cost: expect ~1.5-3x the embedding cost per query depending on top_k and batch size. We'll include cost estimates in the benchmark output.

Recommended test matrix (48-72h automated run)
Arm A — Low latency (POC A):
- Model: redwood-7b-q (int8/quantized)
- Retriever: dense embeddings, embed_model=redwood-embed-2, vector_top_k=30
- Reranker: none (to minimize latency)
- Caching: aggressive prefix caching, TTL=24h
- Targets: latency p50 < 300ms for short queries, precision@1 >= 0.85

Arm B — High accuracy (POC B):
- Model: redwood-13b-std
- Retriever: vector_top_k=50
- Reranker: redwood-reranker-v2 (cross-encoder), reranker_top_n=5
- Chunking: chunk_size=500 tokens, overlap=50
- Targets: precision@1 >= 0.92, hallucination_rate < 3%, latency p50 < 800ms

Evaluation metrics to capture
- Precision@1, MRR, grounding_rate (percent answers citing at least one doc id), hallucination_rate (manual + automated heuristics), latency p50/p95, tokens-per-query cost.

Notes on vector store
- Pinecone: good managed option, consistent low-latency reads; Redwood has a production connector and we can operate the POC with your existing Pinecone instance.
- Milvus (self-hosted): also supported; may give cost advantages at scale but requires customer infra ops.

Next steps
- If ACME is okay, we'll run the 1k prompt-set benchmark against both arms and return a short benchmark report + cost delta.
- I'll include a sample reranker run in the report so you can see the difference in grounding and latency.
- Vivek

Appreciate the context, Sofia — that's exactly what we had in mind. Proposed approach:

1) Two POC arms mapped to user flows
- Support triage (Latency-first): redwood-7b-q, no reranker, heavy caching, vector_top_k=30. Target p50 < 300ms, support concurrency test @200 concurrent small queries.
- Legal/Contracts (Grounding-first): redwood-13b-std + redwood-reranker-v2, vector_top_k=50, reranker_top_n=5. Target precision@1 >= 0.92, p50 < 800ms.

2) Timeline & deliverables
- Nov 25–27: Redwood runs automated benchmark on the 1k prompt set you provide (we'll segment the set into 'support' and 'legal' buckets).
- Nov 30: Benchmark report + recommended config for production + cost estimate.
- Dec 7: Optional workshop to review SOW and rollout plan.

3) SOW / procurement
- We'll put together a short SOW after the benchmark that spells out scope, deliverables, and suggested committed capacity for Dedicated or Hosted API.

Can you confirm the 1k prompt-set share and whether Pinecone will remain the vector store for the POC? Also — Nov 25 after 10am PT is good for a quick sync; I'll send a calendar invite for 10:30am PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
